title: 1971 AHSME Problem 6
statement: Let \(*\) be a symbol denoting the binary operation on the set \(S\) of all nonzero real numbers as follows: for any \(a,\) \(b\in S,\) \(a*b=2ab.\) Which statement is not true?

answerChoices.label: C
answerChoices.text: \(\frac{1}{2}\) is an identity element for \(*\) in \(S\)

answerChoices.label: D
answerChoices.text: Every element of \(S\) has an inverse for \(*\)

answerChoices.label: E
answerChoices.text:
\(\frac{1}{2a}\) is an inverse for \(*\) of the
element \(a\) of \(S\)

solutions.text:
The operation is commutative, and \[ (a*b)*c=4abc=a*(b*c), \] so it is associative. Its identity is \(\frac{1}{2}.\) The inverse of \(a\) must satisfy \(2ax=\frac{1}{2},\) so it is \(x=\frac{1}{4a},\) not \(\frac{1}{2a}.\)

Therefore, the correct answer is E.
